title: Secondary Shares, QMB Protection and Charge Adjustments under Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage
content:
**Rule.** When the tier prohibits balance billing, the resident is never billed any Medicare cost sharing: once the Medicaid crossover remittance for a charge has posted, whatever part of that crossover share the state did not pay is written off against the charge with the reason "QMB balance billing prohibited", and no resident charge is ever raised for it. A QMB write-off is posted only after the Medicaid crossover remittance for that charge has posted. When a Medigap carrier denies its share and the tier rebills secondary denials to the resident, the carrier's charge is reduced with the reason "secondary denial" and the same amount is charged to the resident as a new resident charge naming the denied charge; when the tier does not rebill denials, the share stays with the secondary payer and is followed up after the tier's secondary follow-up days. A charge priced at the wrong year's rate is corrected with the reason "rate-year correction" by the difference, and a split posted under a tier not in effect on the days of service is corrected with the reason "secondary share correction". Reversed covered days reduce the coinsurance charged on them with the day reversal's own reason. An adjustment always names the charge it reduces and never exceeds that charge's open balance.

This is the Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage posting standard for charge adjustments. Whether a tier prohibits balance billing, rebills denials, and after how many days it follows up, are the tier's own figures in the secondary-payer and cost-sharing schedules.

### Adjustment reasons

| Event | Adjustment reason | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Crossover remittance posted, part unpaid by the state (balance billing prohibited) | QMB balance billing prohibited | Unpaid part written off; no resident charge |
| Medigap carrier denies its share, tier rebills denials | Secondary denial | Carrier charge reduced; same amount charged to the resident as a new charge naming the denied charge |
| Charge priced at the wrong year's rate | Rate-year correction | Reduced by the difference |
| Split posted under a tier not in effect on the days of service | Secondary share correction | Corrected |
| Covered days reversed | The day reversal's own reason | Coinsurance on those days reduced |

**Timing gate.** A QMB write-off waits on the Medicaid crossover remittance for that charge being posted, as the system record shows.

**Cap.** An adjustment names the charge it reduces and never exceeds that charge's open balance — its amount less the payments and adjustments posted against it, plus any returned payments.
